scope: v1.3 candidate expansion only; existing v1.2 cases unchanged

findings.evidence: The candidates span finance, logistics, IP, privacy, HR, procurement, IT, and property, and each one changes the causal mechanism rather than only the names or dates.
A few clusters remain close in document family, especially privacy and procurement, but they differ in the controlling fact pattern and the answer mechanism.

Mechanisms include threshold crossing, temporal trigger, scope inclusion, authority coverage, document conflict, document hierarchy, chain completion, missing evidence, multi-document reconciliation, proportional entitlement, exception or waiver, and identity or asset linkage.
The candidate graphs include single-clause documents, two-chain logistics graphs, hierarchy-driven compliance graphs, and conflict-heavy vendor and incident graphs.
The perturbations cover scope changes, time-window shifts, threshold activations, evidence conflicts, missing evidence, liability transfer, conditional rights, and process compliance.
No candidate is a pure renaming of an existing case; the six revised cases were explicitly rewritten to change the reasoning mechanism.

risks: Potential overlap between procure_021 and procure_022 if the final manifests overuse the same procurement checklist template.
Potential overlap between privacy_017 and privacy_018 if both end up using the same legal memo framing.
Potential overlap between hr_019 and approval_chain_009 if the offboarding timing is not made visibly distinct from approval timing.
Potential gold ambiguity in cases that require legal, Incoterms, or deadline knowledge unless the controlling excerpt is embedded.
recommendations: Preserve different document roles for each case even when a shared contract archetype is used.
Require a manual rationale check for all hard cases before gold generation.
Prefer at least one unique document family per case whenever possible.
Avoid reusing the exact same question templates across cases.
